Risk differences use standardized predictions over the eligible analytic population.

The alternative tests nonlinear thresholds and whether MFI’s association changes across VAT levels—information a linear additive model cannot express. It is a flexible descriptive/prognostic surface, not a biological mechanism. Tune smoothing only within the training set via nested participant-level CV; freeze the held-out set. Compare held-out log loss/Brier/calibration and the joint smooth/interaction uncertainty to the baseline, using bootstrap resampling of held-out predictions/participants. Plot adjusted risk contrasts over observed common support; do not extrapolate sparse extremes. If events or common support are inadequate, defer the tensor interaction and report no reliable nonlinear resolution rather than simplifying silently.

A clinically meaningful positive result requires a robust MFI association with interval excluding the null and a prespecified meaningful standardized-risk contrast, directionally consistent across baseline and flexible model, not merely a tiny metric gain. Falsify a distinct signal if the conditional association and standardized risk contrast are near-null with intervals excluding the prespecified minimally important difference, and the flexible model shows no reproducible surface/interaction. If intervals span both meaningful benefit and null/adverse values, call inconclusive. Adverse result (higher MFI associated with lower falls risk) challenges the directional hypothesis and triggers assessment of selection, activity, measurement coding, and survivor bias; it does not imply protective muscle fat. Supportive result justifies replication/clinical adjudication, not causal or intervention claims.

Interpretation threats: MRI cohort selection and survival to repeat assessment may induce collider/healthy-attender bias; restricting to visit-3 responders intensifies this. Preclinical weakness, falls, illness, or declining activity may cause both MFI and subsequent reporting; baseline grip/prior falls and the recall washout reduce but do not remove reverse causation. Self-reported falls has recall/misclassification and visit-specific ascertainment; outcome window avoids overlap but cannot establish event dates or severity. UKB volunteer population limits generalizability. # Prospective muscle-fat signal and falls in UK Biobank

## Scientific question and claim boundary

A recent UK Biobank analysis reports broad associations between MRI thigh muscle fat infiltration (MFI), mortality and incident diseases [K1]. A separate UK Biobank MRI study reports associations between thigh muscle-volume distribution, grip weakness and falls [K2]. Neither inspected abstract establishes that a temporally prior muscle-fat measure predicts a later falls report independently of visceral adiposity (VAT), baseline function and prior falls. The underlying biological interpretation is also disputed: myosteatosis may mark age-related vulnerability or result from disease/disuse, and its imaging measurement lacks a gold standard [K3].

**Hypothesis to test:** Among UKB MRI visit-2 participants with a later visit-3 falls response at least 366 days after visit 2, higher bilateral posterior-thigh MFI at visit 2 will be associated with reporting at least one fall in the year before visit 3, conditional on MRI VAT, muscle volume, general adiposity, age, sex, smoking/activity, and visit-2 grip, walking pace and falls history. The experiment tests an incremental conditional prognostic association, not whether reducing MFI prevents falls or whether MFI is the biological cause.

Falls can cause injury, fracture, disability and loss of independence. A stable temporal MFI signal beyond VAT and baseline function would justify external validation of muscle-quality measures as a way to identify people for functional assessment; a precise null would argue against adding MFI to fall-risk phenotyping despite broad disease associations. Predictive association alone would not establish a screening threshold or treatment decision. Novelty is limited to the specific lagged, head-to-head MFI-versus-VAT and baseline-function contrast; this is not an exhaustive novelty search.

**Evidence versus hypothesis:** The current literature and dataset support field availability and general associations. The independent, time-ordered MFI-to-falls claim remains unresolved. No outcome result has been fit in discovery.

## Population, bindings, and timing

Use the frozen `ukb-completed-subset-20261002`, with source rows read-only. The unit is a single UKB/ukb672073 participant (`eid`). Do not join Olink/dta or ukb671626 identifiers. Main source table is `UKB/ukb672073_Assessment_Center.csv`, source `ukb_d61ec821b81b9034`, exact raw path `[private-path]/ukb672073_Assessment_Center.csv`, catalog SHA-256 `77cad853153b1fdc9b6b9c83b6fff19691681cdee3b0822210bc5c875e1db94c`, source table schema `datasets/population_multiomics/table-fb278a0d71d3a688.json`. Archive member: ordinary CSV file. Use its raw columns, `eid` key; do not use the prepared Assessment Center Parquet derivative for this design because its actual Arrow schema omits `22407` and other MRI columns present in the raw source schema.

- **Primary exposure:** posterior-thigh MFI fields `23355-2.0` (left) and `23356-2.0` (right), each fraction; use their mean after standardizing the two sides in the eligible visit-2 MRI cohort. Field-level values are continuous. Analyze sides separately only as a sensitivity check. Anterior MFI `24353-2.0`/`24354-2.0` is a prespecified secondary region, not part of the primary posterior composite.
- **Comparator/covariates at visit 2:** MRI VAT `22407-2.0` in litres; posterior/anterior thigh fat-free muscle volumes `22403-2.0`–`22406-2.0` in litres; body-fat percentage `23099-2.0`; BMI `21001-2.0`; age at assessment `21003-2.0`; smoking `20116-2.0`; moderate-activity days/week `884-2.0`; usual walking pace `924-2.0`; grip `46-2.0`/`47-2.0` in kg; and baseline-year falls `2296-2.0`. Confirm code labels, units, nonmissing values and any field-quality flags before fitting. Join sex `31-0.0` from `UKB/ukb672073_Population_Characteristics.csv`, source `ukb_ce68812c3a782e09`, path `[private-path]/ukb672073_Population_Characteristics.csv`, schema `table-0f3b3a4749849a80.json`, on same-namespace `eid`; verify unique keys and unmatched counts.
- **Endpoint:** `2296-3.0`, “Falls in the last year,” at the visit-3 assessment, with date `53-3.0`; index date is visit-2 `53-2.0`. Require follow-up date at least 366 days later, so the recalled year before visit 3 begins after the index assessment. The field is a single categorical self-report, not event-level adjudication. Use the exact response-category mapping from coding ID `100539` before classifying yes/no or deriving “any fall”; keep missing, prefer-not-to-answer and other special values distinct from no. Public field metadata confirms the field/coding identifier but the response-code map was not retrieved in discovery. This is an explicit pre-analysis dependency, not an assumption.
- **Secondary outcome:** repeat grip at visit 3, `46-3.0`/`47-3.0`, analyzed as follow-up maximum valid side adjusted for visit-2 maximum grip, not as an unadjusted change alone. It is a continuous functional measure, not adjudicated sarcopenia. Do not substitute it for falls if the falls mapping fails without returning the scientific revision to the Lead.

The full UKB source metadata file is `metadata.csv`, source `ukb_dd10bf7e2be6e7d0`, path `[private-path]/metadata.csv`, schema `table-7cef91a04cb75f7b.json`; relevant dictionary columns are `FieldID`, `Field`, `ValueType`, `Units`, `Instances`, and `Coding`. Its frozen row identifies field 22407 as VAT in litres; MFI fields as fractions; field 2296 as categorical single, four instances, coding 100539. The external code labels remain required.

### Bounded data feasibility already observed

A read-only Arrow scan of all 502,370 rows in the raw Assessment Center source used projected fields and wrote aggregate counts only. It found 39,419 with visit-2 VAT, four MFI-region measures and date nonempty; 4,962 had a parsed visit-3 date at least 366 days later; 4,920 had a nonempty visit-3 falls response; and 4,665 had grip fields at both visits. Of 4,962 lag-qualified participants, 292 were 366–729 days apart and 4,670 were at least 730 days apart. Raw visit-3 falls codes were `1: 4,121`, `2: 583`, `3: 213`, `-3: 3`; these are values only, not classified events/controls. The date windows do not overlap for the lag-qualified cohort. This supports basic field/temporal feasibility but is not an analytic cohort size or an outcome result. Prior-falls category counts, final covariate-complete N, duplicate-`eid` check, join audit, MRI quality-flag review, response mapping and event support remain to be checked before model fitting. The source schema is rich and no sampling was performed in the scan.

## Estimand and computable Harbor experiment

Primary estimand: adjusted odds ratio and standardized risk difference in visit-3 report of any fall per one-SD higher visit-2 posterior-thigh MFI, conditional on visit-2 VAT, thigh muscle volume, body adiposity, age, sex, smoking, activity, interval, baseline grip/walking pace and prior-year falls. Preserve common cohort and make prior falls a categorical covariate after codebook decoding; prespecified sensitivity excludes participants with prior-year falls. Do not call this incident fall timing at exact event level—the outcome is a recall window after baseline.

1. Before modeling, verify official category codes for 2296/coding 100539, units/ranges, repeated column values, MRI quality flags, duplicate IDs, visit ordering, missingness, response and covariate overlap. Produce a cohort-flow table and category counts. If the code map cannot be verified, stop falls modeling and report the blocked dependency; do not infer “no fall” from code 1 or any other raw code.
2. Fit an interpretable logistic baseline: age, sex, interval, baseline falls/function, VAT, general adiposity, thigh volume, smoking and activity. Then add standardized posterior-thigh MFI. Report MFI coefficient, OR, 95% CI, adjusted standardized risk differences, calibration and Brier score with bootstrap uncertainty. Compare the incremental MFI term to the same baseline covariates without MFI. Use the minimum clinical effect margin only if a falls/musculoskeletal expert prespecifies it; otherwise report statistical uncertainty without declaring clinical utility.
3. Fit a same-question GAM/logistic alternative with restricted cubic splines for MFI and VAT and a prespecified MFI×VAT interaction. It tests whether thresholds or joint adiposity contexts hidden by a linear additive model are present; it is not included just to maximize prediction. Use participant-level stratified fivefold evaluation, keep all preprocessing within folds, and compare out-of-fold Brier/calibration and discrimination with bootstrap uncertainty. No external validation is available in this UKB snapshot.
4. Prespecified sensitivity analyses: baseline prior-fall stratification/exclusion; posterior versus anterior MFI; with/without thigh volume (changes the conditional estimand); body-fat versus BMI adjustment to avoid redundant adjustment; and continuous repeat grip outcome. Account for follow-up nonresponse descriptively; MRI/re-attendance selection cannot be eliminated by complete-case analysis. Do not code missing falls as none.

**Scientific deliverable:** newly fit the adjusted logistic baseline and MFI-augmented model, fit the prespecified nonlinear interaction model if event support allows, and return the cohort-flow/coding audit, event support, coefficient/risk-contrast tables with intervals, risk-shape plots, and held-out calibration/Brier/AUC outputs with uncertainty. If the coding dependency or minimum effective event support fails, a documented stop/deferral is an acceptable outcome; no alternate endpoint or narrowed population may be substituted mechanically.

## Rival explanations, falsification, and interpretation

The leading explanation is that posterior-thigh MFI marks muscle-quality vulnerability not represented by abdominal VAT. The strongest rival is that MFI reflects overall adiposity, age, low activity/disuse, pre-existing weakness, chronic disease, recall/measurement practices, or selection into and return to MRI; any association can be confounded or reverse-causal. Adjusting baseline function, falls and adiposity plus the nonoverlapping report window separates some observable predictions, but it cannot remove unmeasured/time-varying confounding or healthy-attender selection. UKB imaging returnees are not a representative clinical cohort.

- **Supportive:** a positive, reasonably precise adjusted MFI association remains after VAT and baseline function/history, with stable direction in prespecified sensitivities; the MFI term improves held-out calibration/risk estimation beyond the conventional covariate model. This supports a distinct prognostic association in selected UKB returnees and motivates external validation, not a mechanism, causality, treatment effect, or clinical threshold.
- **Adverse:** with adequate events and precision, the adjusted MFI association is null/opposite or too small to meet a clinician-prespecified meaningful margin, while VAT/baseline function/history accounts for the signal and the flexible alternative finds no stable nonlinear/subgroup pattern. This weakens this particular added falls-risk signal, not all biology of myosteatosis.
- **Inconclusive:** wide intervals, sparse outcomes, uncertain code mapping, poor overlap, unstable estimates, or substantial nonresponse/selection sensitivity. Do not treat an imprecise null as refutation.

Computationally checkable outputs include cohort filters, field joins, code use, model fitting, estimates, uncertainty calculations and whether conclusions accurately follow from computed output. Automatic verification cannot decide whether a self-report corresponds to a clinically adjudicated fall, whether the effect is clinically meaningful without an expert-set margin, or whether MFI causes functional decline. Stronger claims need adjudicated fall dates/severity or prospective surveillance, MFI algorithm/quality review, physical-activity and time-varying disease evidence, an external cohort, and ultimately intervention or mechanistic evidence.

## Method comparison, compute, and deferred paths

**Simple baseline:** adjusted logistic regression with linear standardized predictors and an explicit comparison of the model without versus with MFI. Inputs are the exact visit-2 fields above; fitting target is verified visit-3 any-fall self-report. Use the complete eligible participant cohort for inference, bootstrap intervals, and participant-level stratified fivefold prediction evaluation. This is transparent and clinically interpretable for a single prespecified question.

**Substantive alternative:** GAM with smooth terms for MFI and VAT plus an interaction, same participant rows/input variables/target/folds, and nested preprocessing. It could reveal thresholds or an MFI effect concentrated at high VAT that linear main effects miss. Uncertainty and calibration/Brier plus discrimination are reported; predictive gain alone is not a clinical-value argument. If the outcome coding/support cannot sustain spline degrees of freedom, defer the alternative rather than changing population or endpoint.

A neural sequence model is deferred for a question-specific reason: two sparse imaging/function visits and one later recall item do not provide dense longitudinal sequences that would distinguish disease ordering; it would not solve reverse causation or selection. Delphi's disease-sequence method and ALADYNOULLI longitudinal latent trajectories remain revisit candidates only if a later question has adequate dated trajectories. The Oncoformer demonstration is not pursued because this is not a cancer/image-payload question; its unavailable main-paper methods are not assumed from the supplement. These are dispositions, not general method bans.

The solver planning envelope in `inputs.json` is 16 CPUs, 256 GiB, 8 GPUs and 8 hours. This is a small tabular task; request zero GPUs. Estimate 2–8 CPU-hours for source extraction/quality checks, logistic/GAM fits, bootstrap and fivefold evaluation (unmeasured; confirm at readiness). Discovery diagnostics were small bounded CPU scans, not a completed scientific analysis. No proposer/solver training or solver study was run.

## Key works

[K1] Zhang et al. report broad associations of UKB thigh MFI with mortality/incident diseases and multi-omics signals. This already bounds broad novelty; the added question is the lagged falls-specific MFI-versus-VAT contrast adjusted for baseline function. Only the Europe PMC abstract was inspected; acquired full-text XML was unreadable in discovery, so no methods/full-text claim is made.

[K2] Kim et al. report a neck-to-knee MRI muscle-volume/distribution framework and associations with grip, falls and mortality in UKB. This supports thigh phenotyping relevance but does not establish the proposed MFI-specific temporal contrast or causality. Publisher abstract/introduction excerpt inspected, not full paper.

[K3] Roe et al. review myosteatosis evidence and state that disease/disuse versus aging remains uncertain and that imaging has no gold-standard measure. Relevant abstract/section-1 excerpt inspected; this bounds interpretation, not direct evidence for this hypothesis.

Bibliography receipts and source excerpts, with exact attached-byte hashes, are in `supporting/key-references.json`, `supporting/K1-Zhang-et-al-2026-EuropePMC-abstract.txt`, `supporting/K2-Kim-et-al-2026-publisher-excerpt.txt`, and `supporting/K3-Roe-et-al-2026-publisher-excerpt.txt`.

A review identifies unresolved disease/disuse versus aging explanations and nonstandard imaging measures [K3]. These works support the question's relevance, not the hypothesis's truth or novelty beyond this specific contrast. K1 was inspected as an Europe PMC abstract only; K2 as publisher abstract/introduction passages; K3 as abstract/section 1. Limits and byte-hashed receipts are preserved in `supporting/key-references.json` and the three attached source excerpts.

Falls can lead to injury, fracture, disability and loss of independence. A robust MFI association distinct from VAT and baseline function would justify external validation of muscle-quality phenotyping for functional risk assessment; a precise near-null would argue against adding this MRI measure to falls phenotyping. The result is neither a validated screening threshold nor evidence that changing MFI prevents falls. This proposal tests an association/prediction claim, not mechanism or causality. # Lead working proposal — does MFI add to thigh-muscle distribution for later falls?

## Question and why it matters

A 2026 UK Biobank study reports that posterior/anterior (P/A) thigh muscle-volume ratio is associated with falls cross-sectionally. The parent question—whether MRI posterior-thigh fat infiltration predicts later falls—remains different in exposure and time ordering, but it should now explicitly test whether MFI adds information beyond this closest anatomical comparator. The clinical uncertainty is whether MFI offers distinct muscle-quality information, or merely restates regional muscle-volume distribution/frailty.

**Hypothesis:** among UKB imaging visit-2 participants with a valid visit-3 falls response at least 366 days later, higher bilateral posterior-thigh MFI at visit 2 is positively associated with any fall reported for the year before visit 3 after adjustment for VAT, total thigh fat-free volume, P/A muscle-volume ratio, prior falls, baseline function, adiposity, age, sex, smoking and activity. This is a conditional prognostic association in selected returnees, not a causal or mechanistic effect. A positive conditional MFI association beyond P/A ratio would distinguish composition from mass distribution; a precise null would suggest no additional MFI signal for this endpoint beyond the closest prior MRI phenotype.

**Strong rival:** MFI is a marker of frailty, inactivity/disuse, adiposity, illness or prior falls; the published P/A ratio may capture the relevant functional anatomy. Selection into MRI/return visits, reporting opportunity, recall and measurement error can also induce/attenuate associations. Adjustment/time order cannot eliminate these explanations.

Falls can lead to injury, fracture, disability and loss of independence. A robust distinct MFI signal warrants external validation for functional-risk phenotyping; a precise near-null argues against prioritizing an extra MRI composition metric. Neither changes treatment or screening without validated utility and intervention evidence.

## Evidence boundary and closest works

Strongest supported evidence: UKB has the source fields and visit dates needed for the proposed bounded retrospective-report association; a previous aggregate-only overlap screen found 4,962 participants with ≥366-day visit separation and nonempty follow-up responses before code classification. This is not a complete-case cohort, event count, model fit or result.

The 2026 Kim et al. UKB study [K2] reports cross-sectional association of P/A thigh muscle-volume ratio with falls; in publisher-text passages inspected this episode, the sample is 37,004 age >50 with MRI/grip/DEXA, but complete methods were not audited. It bounds broad novelty of thigh-MRI/falls associations, not the proposed MFI-specific, temporally ordered conditional comparison. Zhang et al. [K1] is an Europe PMC abstract only and reports broad UKB MFI-health associations, not a verified falls-specific result. Roe et al. [K3] is an abstract/section-1 review excerpt and motivates caution about age versus disease/disuse and imaging heterogeneity. These are three distinct inspected works, and not proof of novelty. It cannot adjudicate falls, decide the meaningful clinical margin, certify MRI quality, remove unmeasured confounding, infer mechanism/causality or establish clinical utility. Those stronger claims need expert review, objective/event-level falls data, external cohort validation and an intervention or mechanistic study.

## Method/reference disposition

The linear nested logistic model is the interpretable baseline, while the GAM addresses nonlinear MFI and MFI×P/A effect-modification uncertainty on identical inputs/validation. The sequence-model demonstrations Delphi and ALADYNOULLI are not selected because this question is sparse imaging/function at two visits rather than disease-order or latent trajectory learning; Oncoformer is not selected because multimodal cancer imaging/EHR inputs are irrelevant and its main text/full methods were unavailable in the demonstration bundle. These are question-specific deferrals, not blanket method bans. The three works above are the proposal's sole key-reference set [K1]–[K3]; key-reference JSON and inspected evidence files attach unchanged from the parent.

The key inferential test is MFI's conditional coefficient/95% CI; report standardized absolute risk contrasts if supported, calibration/Brier and participant-level stratified five-fold out-of-fold prediction. This is not causal.

Scientifically substantive alternative: a shrinkage-controlled generalized additive logistic fit on the exact same cohort, outcome and folds, with smooth MFI and P/A ratio terms plus their prespecified interaction (and smooth VAT). It tests whether the MFI signal is nonlinear or concentrated in a particular muscle-distribution pattern, information a single linear term loses. Compare uncertainty-supported conditional curves/joint test and calibration/log-loss/Brier; do not select it for a small score gain. If event support/denominator quality cannot sustain it, defer the flexible fit and label the comparison inconclusive rather than changing population or endpoint. Small tabular analysis: CPU, no GPU; planned but unmeasured full solver estimate 2–8 CPU-hours extraction/QC/fits/folds/bootstrap, within `inputs.json` solver envelope (16 CPU, 256 GiB, 28,800 s). No outcomes were fitted during discovery.

Supportive: adjusted MFI association is positive, reasonably precise, robust to prespecified coding/missingness/selection checks and remains beyond P/A distribution, VAT and function; this warrants independent validation only. Adverse: sufficiently precise near-null/opposite MFI estimate excludes a clinical-reviewer-defined meaningful margin and no stable GAM pattern remains, supporting not prioritizing MFI for this specific falls-phenotyping use—not refuting all myosteatosis biology. Inconclusive: sparse outcomes, wide intervals, invalid/unstable ratio, coding anomalies, missingness/selection sensitivity or unstable flexible terms. An imprecise null is not falsification.

Computational verifier can test source bindings, filters, keys, code mapping, P/A derivation, counts, models, uncertainty and whether conclusions track computed outputs. It cannot adjudicate falls, decide the meaningful clinical margin, certify MRI quality, remove unmeasured confounding, infer mechanism/causality or establish clinical utility. Those stronger claims need expert review, objective/event-level falls data, external cohort validation and an intervention or mechanistic study.

## Method/reference disposition

The linear nested logistic model is the interpretable baseline, while the GAM addresses nonlinear MFI and MFI×P/A effect-modification uncertainty on identical inputs/validation. The sequence-model demonstrations Delphi and ALADYNOULLI are not selected because this question is sparse imaging/function at two visits rather than disease-order or latent trajectory learning; Oncoformer is not selected because multimodal cancer imaging/EHR inputs are irrelevant and its main text/full methods were unavailable in the demonstration bundle. These are question-specific deferrals, not blanket method bans. The three works above are the proposal's sole key-reference set [K1]–[K3]; key-reference JSON and inspected evidence files attach unchanged from the parent.
